dtc.html: at a glance what you get a credit that lowers your income tax, and the approval other programs ask for. for the 2025 tax year the disability amount is $10,138 , plus $5,914 more for a child under 18. who it is for anyone whose doctor or nurse practitioner can certify a severe, long-lasting impairment. there is no income test and no age limit. children, working adults and seniors all qualify. what it costs nothing to apply. some practitioners charge a fee to fill in their part of the form. that fee can be claimed as a medical expense. how long it takes an appointment with your practitioner, plus the form. the canada revenue agency then reviews it and writes to you with a yes or a no. you need this first nothing. this is the first step. everything else comes after it. what is on this page what the disability tax credit is what it unlocks who qualifies how much it is worth how to apply, step by step claiming up to 10 past years if you are turned down why people miss this where to get help in victoria related guides where these numbers come from what the disability tax credit is the disability tax credit — most people say dtc — is a credit on your income tax. it lowers the tax you owe if you have a serious impairment that has lasted, or is expected to last, a long time. it is non-refundable . that is tax language for: it can bring your tax bill down, but it does not come to you as a cheque on its own. if you do not owe enough tax to use it all, the leftover amount can be moved to a spouse, parent, child or other close relative who supports you. to get it, a medical practitioner fills in part of a form called t2201 , and the canada revenue agency (cra) decides yes or no. what it unlocks this is the real reason to apply, and almost nobody is told it. being approved for the dtc is what makes you eligible for a list of other programs. without it, the door stays shut. the canada disability benefit — a monthly federal payment for people aged 18 to 64. you cannot get it without the dtc. the registered disability savings plan (rdsp) — where the government pays up to $1,000 a year into a savings plan for you, even if you never deposit a dollar. the child disability benefit — extra monthly money for a family raising a child who has the dtc. the canada workers benefit disability supplement — extra money for people with the dtc who are working. the home accessibility tax credit — help with the cost of making a home safer to live in. good news even if you pay no income tax at all, the dtc is still worth applying for . the approval itself is the thing. it is what the canada disability benefit and the rdsp both check for. who qualifies a medical practitioner has to certify that your impairment is severe and prolonged . in plain words: it is serious, and it is not going away soon. the cra looks at whether you have: a marked restriction in one of these areas — walking, mental functions, dressing, feeding, eliminating (bowel or bladder), hearing, speaking, or vision; or significant limits in two or more of those areas that, added together, are as bad as one marked restriction; or you need life-sustaining therapy — for example some people with type 1 diabetes, or people on dialysis. there is no income test. there is no age limit. a child can qualify, a working person can qualify, and a senior can qualify. "mental functions" counts memory, concentration, judgment, mood, and the ability to manage yourself day to day all sit under "mental functions". a lot of people with mental illness, brain injury, dementia or long-term chronic pain never apply because they picture a wheelchair. the test is about daily living, not about whether you can work. how much it is worth these are the amounts you write on your tax return. the money you actually save is a percentage of them, not the whole number, so check the current amount for your own situation with the cra or a free tax clinic. disability amount, 2025 tax year who amount on the return adult $10,138 child under 18 $10,138 plus a supplement of $5,914 — $16,052 in total when you are approved, the amount goes on line 31600 of your own return. if it is being transferred from a dependant, it goes on line 31800. from a spouse or common-law partner, line 32600. a free tax clinic will put it in the right place for you. how to apply, step by step pick the right practitioner. a doctor or nurse practitioner can certify any impairment. for specific ones, so can an optometrist (vision), an audiologist (hearing), an occupational therapist (walking, feeding, dressing), a physiotherapist (walking), a psychologist (mental functions) or a speech-language pathologist (speaking). book the appointment and say what it is for. ask for the disability tax credit certificate, form t2201. do not just drop the form at the front desk with no explanation. fill in part a yourself. that is the applicant's part. you can do it online in cra my account, by phone with the cra, or on the paper form. your practitioner fills in part b. this is the part that decides the answer. both parts must be done the same way — all digital, or all paper. do not mix them. send any other charge for a service it is required to provide. it also works the other way round. if your own disability means one seat is not enough for you, the second seat is free as well. what this is worth a return flight from victoria to toronto for a support person can easily be $700 or more. under this rule you pay the taxes and a few fees on that seat, not the fare. on a family that travels once or twice a year for medical care, that is real money. free of fare is not free of everything the canadian transportation agency cannot stop an airline charging government taxes on the extra seat. that includes the air travellers security charge and federal and provincial taxes. some airlines absorb them anyway. airports are expected to absorb their airport improvement fee for a support person. so when you ask, ask this: "what exactly will the second seat cost me, all in?" a number like $40 in taxes is normal. a number like $400 means someone has charged you a fare. three limits are worth knowing before you plan anything: it is for travel inside canada only. victoria to calgary, yes. victoria to seattle, no. a flight abroad is not covered, even on a canadian airline. it binds large airlines. the law defines a large airline as one that carried a million passengers or more worldwide in each of the two years before. small carriers are not bound by this part of the law. you have to ask ahead. the law gives the airline a deadline only if you ask at least 48 hours before departure. ask later and it becomes a favour, not a right. the three ways to qualify the rules set out three separate doors. you only need one of them. free additional seating on flights within canada door who it covers what you have to show a support person you need help during the flight itself with people on disability assistance in bc believe that the first paycheque takes the cheque away. it is the single most common reason people never try. it is not how the rules work. bc gives every person government says it plainly: you always keep 100% of the money you earn. even if you earn more than the exemption, your wages are yours. it is only the assistance payment that goes down, and only by the amount you went over. you also do not have to work. having the pwd designation means the ministry does not require you to look for a job or sign a work plan. if you want an employability plan, you can ask for one. nobody can make you. the $16,200 a year you can earn these are the limits from 1 january 2026. they cover money you earn from a job or from self-employment. bc annual earnings
